notes: The instance is password-protected from the first start: AUTH_TOKEN (generated) is the password and JWT_SECRET (generated) signs the sessions, so a public site never opens on an unclaimed setup screen. Sign in with the password shown here.
To give people their own logins, switch to multi-user mode in Settings → Security: you create the administrator account there, and after that everyone signs in with a username and password.

AnythingLLM keeps its settings (the LLM and embedder you pick, API keys, the password) in a .env file. Upstream bind-mounts that file from the host; here it lives on the data volume (/app/server/storage/.env) and the start command links it into place, so settings survive a container re-create. The generated password and JWT secret are written into that file only on the very first start, which means a password you change (or turn off) in Settings → Security stays changed.

No model is bundled. Pick an LLM provider and enter its API key during onboarding or later in Settings → AI Providers. The built-in embedder (it runs on the CPU and downloads a small model on first use) and the built-in LanceDB vector store need no extra service.

Web page import works without extra privileges: upstream asks for the SYS_ADMIN capability only so that the Chromium browser behind its website scraper can use its sandbox. This recipe adds no privileges and runs that browser unsandboxed instead (ANYTHINGLLM_CHROMIUM_ARGS), inside the app's own container.

The container starts as root only to hand the data volume to the image's anythingllm user and to link the .env file; the app itself runs as anythingllm (setpriv). Anonymous telemetry is turned off (DISABLE_TELEMETRY).
Everything (documents, vectors, the SQLite database, downloaded models and the settings file) lives in one named volume on /app/server/storage.
